Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION NO. MR. REN JINHUA Chairman of the Board Philippine Infradev Holdings, Inc. 6784 Ayala Avenue, Makati City Dear Mr. Jinhua: This has reference to your letter dated 3 September 2019, seeking this Department's authorization that Mayor Benjamin Magalong of Baguio City be allowed to continue his directorship with Philippine Infradev Holdings, Inc. At the outset, attention is invited to the pertinent provision of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160), specifically Section 90 thereof which provides, viz: "Section 90. Practice of Profession. - (a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. (Emphasis supplied) Clearly, the afore-quoted provision prohibits governors, city/municipal mayors from practicing their profession or engage in any other occupation during his incumbency. As bolstered in the case of Catu vs. Rellosa (A.C. No. 5738, dated 19 February 2008), the Supreme Court had elucidated the rationale of such prohibition, thus: "xxx governors, city mayors and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. This is because they are required to render full time service. They should therefore devote all their time and attention to the performance of their official duties. " (Emphasis supplied) On this, we deemed it necessary to indulge a discussion on what constitutes "practice of profession" and "engage in any occupation". This Department, in its Legal Opinion No. 5 series of 2019, had this to say: "xxx it bears to note that the Local Government Code of 1991 did not define the phrase "practice of profession" not did it define the

phrase "engage in any occupation". Hence, the general rule in construing words and phrases used in law (in the) absence of a legislative intent to the contrary, it should be given their plain, ordinary, and common meaning. Hence, in the furtherance of this discussion, we deemed it proper to revisit the meaning of the words tangent to our elucidation, Webster Dictionary defines profession as a calling requiring specialized knowledge and often long and intensive academic preparation. On the other hand, occupation has been commonly defined as an activity in which one is engaged into. Hence, apparently, there is a distinction between the two in that, to exercise profession means that one has to be academically prepared, take the government examination and pass it and is registered in a government licensing body which regulates such profession. On the other hand, when one's activity does not fall within the ambit of "exercise of profession", the same can properly fall under engage in any occupation. " xxx" Since the rationale behind the prohibition in Section 90 of the LGC is to ensure that governors, city/municipal mayors extend their undivided attention and must devote their full time only in discharging their duties and functions being the highest official of the province, city/municipality, we are of the view that what Section 90 Of the Local Government Code of 1991 only requires is only divestment of management of your shareholdings in the corporation, not divestment of title/ownership thereto. Divestment of management entails non-attendance to shareholders meeting and other regular functions of a shareholder while divestment of title/ownership already requires full disposal of shares (e.g. through sale) therein. Having such context in mind, it is important that we define the term "Independent Director". Section 22 (c) of Republic Act No. 11232, otherwise known as the "Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines" defined Independent Director as: "a person who, apart from shareholdings and fees received from the corporation, is independent of management and free from any business or other relationship which could, or could reasonably be perceived to materially interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities as a director. " From the foregoing, we can discern that an Independent Director is essentially independent from the management and operation of a company. He lacks official, professional or business connection with the Management. In that regard, we are of the considered view that Mayor Magalong may be allowed to continue his independent directorship with Philippine Infradev Holdings Inc., as he will not actively participate in its management and daily operation. DILG Opinion No. 26, series of 2013, dated 7 August 2013

However, if there is a conflict of interest on the part of Mayor Magalong with the corporation to which he has shareholders, please be advised that such divestment of management is no longer sufficient. Conflict of interest arises when a public official or employee is a member Of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty.2 When there is a conflict of interest, Section 90 of the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards requires the public official concerned to resign from his position in the private business enterprise within thirty (30) days from his assumption to office and or divest himself of his shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from such assumption, thus: "Section 9. Divestment. - A public official or employee shall avoid conflicts of interest at all times. When a conflict of interest arises, he shall resign from his position in any private business enterprise within thirty (30) days from his assumption of office and/or divest himself of his shareholdings or interest within sixty (60) days from such assumption. The same rule shall apply where the public official or employee is a partner in a partnership. The requirement of divestment shall not apply to those who serve the Government in an honorary capacity nor to laborers and casual or temporary workers. " We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, By t e authority of the ecretary MARIV C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Un rsecretary for Local Government Legal,'27 MARLO L. IRINGAN, CESO 111 Regional Director DILG-CAR ATTY. ODILON L.
